A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NVILA work, with readable text, figures, tables, equations, and appendix Table A1. V2's unresolved PixMo table reference is an identifiable reporting deficiency; it does not prevent comparison of the supplied content.

before.justification: V1 reports original NVILA benchmark results, compression and pruning experiments, fine-tuning measurements, and training/deployment efficiency results.

after.justification: V2 retains original NVILA experiments and adds learning-rate controls, comparison results, and revised application measurements.

M1.justification: The SigLIP–MLP–Qwen2 architecture, Dynamic-S2, spatial/temporal compression, DeltaLoss, FP8 training, and deployment quantization remain unchanged. The expanded learning-rate comparison tests the existing fine-tuning recipe.

E1.justification: The benchmark tasks, application domains, and appendix data recipe are retained. Table 5 names the datasets underlying v1's retained five-benchmark aggregate. Molmo/PixMo data already appears in v1's Table A1, so the new pruning discussion does not establish expanded dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds Florence-VL to the image comparison, InternVL2 to the video comparison, VILA-1.5 to temporal localization, and VILA-M3 to the medical comparison (Tables 8–10 and 12). These extend existing comparator sets. Table 9's empty VILA-1.5 row supplies no evaluated results.

E3.justification: Table 5 adds equal-learning-rate controls, and Table 10 adds a matched-data VILA/NVILA backbone comparison. Table 12 introduces BLEU-4 evaluation for report generation. The main NVILA training pipeline and benchmark splits remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds controlled evidence for different ViT/LLM learning rates. Section 2.2.1 adds qualitative findings about PixMo mixing and pruning, although its referenced 'Table??' is absent. V1's cumulative training-cost breakdown and fabric-folding video comparison are removed; the central compression, pruning, and precision ablations remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging three random-pruning runs. There is no change to repeated-run information, seed disclosure, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Training-efficiency and application evidence are substantially revised. Figure 1 now reports 80/208 H100 GPU-days and 5.1×/1.9× speedups for image/video training, replacing v1's 4.5× summary. Table 11 changes NVILA's SR/SPL from 42.5/36.6 to 53.3/48.8; Table 12 replaces medical results, including Rad accuracy 90.4 to 85.5, and adds BLEU-4. Control/comparator entries are added and NVILA-Lite video results removed. Principal NVILA image/video benchmark scores remain unchanged. Unexplained downstream revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: The DeltaLoss definition in Equation (1) and existing mathematical reasoning are retained. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace the 4.5× training-cost claim with 1.9–5.1× and omit the headline 3.4× fine-tuning memory reduction. Figure 1 distinguishes image and video training. The central efficiency/accuracy contribution and application claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 interprets PixMo mixing as evidence that enlarging training sets can hurt performance and that pruning mitigates this. Table 12 removes v1's qualification that some Med-Gemini results involve subsets or undisclosed preprocessing, while retaining the corresponding baseline values.

D1.justification: V2 documents the five fine-tuning datasets, learning-rate search grid, localization frame counts/data matching, and RGB-only navigation inputs. It removes fine-tuning image/patch/context specifications, medical expert-card details, and the PDFA access URL. The abstract/introduction now state that code and models are available, although the conclusion still promises future availability. Core training details and Table A1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: References are added for medical Gemini, mixed-precision training, fine-tuning benchmarks, MLVU/MVBench, and Video-XL/Oryx. Existing research-positioning and novelty arguments remain essentially unchanged; many other reference edits update formatting or bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: Localized prose and caption edits accompany revised section titles, terminology such as Image-10 to IM-10, author/affiliation changes, and bibliographic cleanup. The overall section order and narrative remain. V2 introduces unresolved table and figure references.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned, qualitative figures are merged with one example removed, and the medical workflow figure is deleted. Several figures move or are renumbered. Tables 5, 6, 8, and 10–12 are structurally reworked, including separate MMMU columns and explicit control, configuration, and metric columns. These changes substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Clearer image/video training-cost reporting and the added controls in Tables 5 and 10 strengthen empirical support. However, the new PixMo finding lacks its referenced table, medical comparability caveats disappear, and some reproducibility details are lost. With the central method and principal benchmark results unchanged, these substantive benefits and reporting regressions leave the net quality effect uncertain.
